title: How good does a cloth simulator have to be before the laundry-robot hanger it designs is the right one?
lede: research programme: how much cloth-simulator fidelity and fabric data a laundry-robot hanger design loop needs before its choice holds on a validated solver; milestone 1, on four fabrics with published KES-FB bending rigidity and weight, finds the 2D chain and 3D sheet agree on every decision (wood-shaped hanger, arm 1 cm wider than the half shoulder) but agree to 0.004 cm because on a deep arm they are one model, and on a 3 cm arm the solver error (0.05 to 0.11 cm) is as large as the margin that picks the width (0.08 to 0.13 cm)
summary: An open research programme on designing a laundry robot's hangers by cloth simulation: how much simulator fidelity and how much measured fabric data the design loop needs before the hanger it picks is still the best one on a validated, calibrated solver, and whether cheap models can certify that. The proposal reviews 19 works (cloth solvers, cloth parameter fitting, the cloth sim-to-real gap, multi-fidelity and robust design), states four falsifiable hypotheses and targets IEEE RA-L. Milestone 1 scores three stock hangers and five arm widths on four fabrics whose bending rigidity (0.0066 to 0.125 gf·cm²/cm) and weight are published KES-FB measurements, in three model tiers (2D chain, 3D sheet on a slab arm, 3D sheet on a 3 cm half-depth arm scored on the whole sheet). Every tier picks the wood-shaped hanger (0.38 to 0.47 cm RMS from the worn shape on the slab, against 3.1 to 3.4 cm for wire and plastic) and an arm 1 cm wider than the half shoulder on every fabric; the only ranking disagreement is a tie for second place. But on a deep arm the 2D and 3D errors differ by at most 0.004 cm, so their agreement is no test of fidelity, and on the 3 cm arm doubling the solver iterations moves the error by 0.05 to 0.11 cm, the same size as the 0.08 to 0.13 cm margin that decides the width. Simulation only: stretch stiffness (150 N/m) is assumed, garments are one size-M strip, there is no friction and no validated solver yet.
